questions.title: What open() Returns
questions.description: What does the expression open("data.txt", "r") evaluate to?
questions.Option1: A file object that you can read from and should close afterwards
questions.Option2: The file's entire text content as one string
questions.Option3: A list of the file's lines

questions.title: Write Mode Truncates
questions.description: What happens to an existing file's content when you open it with mode "w"?
questions.Option1: The existing content is wiped (the file is truncated) immediately
questions.Option2: New writes are appended after the existing content
questions.Option3: Opening fails if the file already exists

questions.title: Append Mode Behavior
questions.description: Which statement about opening a file with mode "a" is true?
questions.Option1: Every write goes to the end of the file and existing content is kept
questions.Option2: The file is truncated before the first write
questions.Option3: It reads the file from the last line backwards
questions.Option4: It creates a timestamped copy of the file

questions.title: with Statement Auto-Close
questions.description: What does the with statement guarantee about a file opened in its header?
questions.Option1: It is closed automatically when the block exits, even if an exception occurs
questions.Option2: It stays open until the whole program exits
questions.Option3: It is flushed to disk after every single write call
questions.Option4: It becomes read-only for the duration of the block

questions.title: Second Read After EOF
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print?
questions.codesnippet:
with open("/tmp/mcq20_eof.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("hello")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_eof.txt") as f:
    a = f.read()
    b = f.read()
print(len(a), len(b))

questions.description: What does opening a file with mode "x" do?
questions.Option1: Creates a new file for writing but fails with FileExistsError if it already exists
questions.Option2: Truncates any existing file and opens it for writing
questions.Option3: Opens the file for appending only

questions.Option2: It converts the file to binary format
questions.Option3: It deletes the file from disk
questions.Option4: It compresses the file for faster reads

questions.title: Truncate on Rewrite
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print?
questions.codesnippet:
with open("/tmp/mcq20_trunc.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("old data")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_trunc.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("new")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_trunc.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())

questions.title: Line Length Tally
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print? (Remember: iterating a file yields lines WITH their newline characters.)
questions.codesnippet:
with open("/tmp/mcq20_iter.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("a\nb\nc")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_iter.txt") as f:
    total = 0
    for line in f:
        total += len(line)
print(total)

questions.title: Append After Write
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print?
questions.codesnippet:
with open("/tmp/mcq20_app.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("A")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_app.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("B")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_app.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())

questions.title: Readline Progression
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print? (readline() advances the file cursor.)
questions.Option1: one then two, on two separate lines
questions.Option2: one twice, on two separate lines
questions.Option3: one, two and three, on three lines
questions.codesnippet:
with open("/tmp/mcq20_rl.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("one\ntwo\nthree")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_rl.txt") as f:
    print(f.readline().strip())
    print(f.readline().strip())

questions.title: readlines Shape
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print?
questions.codesnippet:

    f.write("p\nq\nr")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_rall.txt") as f:

questions.title: seek and tell Walk
questions.description: What does this Python snippet print (three lines)?
questions.Option1: 0, then 2, then abc — on three lines
questions.Option2: 0, then 2, then def — on three lines
questions.Option3: 2, then 4, then abc — on three lines
questions.Option4: 0, then 0, then abc — on three lines
questions.codesnippet:
with open("/tmp/mcq20_seek.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("abcdef")
with open("/tmp/mcq20_seek.txt") as f:
    print(f.tell())
    f.read(2)
    print(f.tell())
    f.seek(0)
    print(f.read(3))

questions.title: Meaning of r+ Mode
questions.description: What does opening an existing file with mode "r+" do?
questions.Option1: Opens it for reading AND writing without truncating; the file must already exist
questions.Option2: Reads the whole file, then truncates it to zero length
questions.Option3: Opens a binary file for reading only
questions.Option4: Creates a new file exclusively for reading and writing
